design_note: Beijing airport operator financial-state sample. Version 0.7 separates short-term policy-rate and long-term 10-year-yield loan benchmarks and persists the fixed-at-draw quote decomposition. Version 0.6 added quarterly income-tax prepayment, Q4 annual tax settlement, and 5-year tax-loss carryforward. Quarterly operations profit is treated as pre-depreciation operating profit; this layer subtracts accounting depreciation, rebuild demolition expense, rebuild old-asset writeoffs, interest expense, and income tax to update retained earnings.

game_timeline.design_note: 2025-2029 is automatic operating history. The player starts in 2030, with the first player-phase commercial contract cycle also beginning in 2030.

opening_balance.design_note: Opening cash is a game-calibrated 2025 balance. It is deliberately large enough for normal operations and the first sample renovation, but not so large that late new-build capex becomes irrelevant. Opening contributed capital is auto-balanced from opening cash plus 2025 opening asset book value.

tax_policy.design_note: Simplified single-player tax model: positive quarterly pretax profit is prepaid at 25%; Q4 settles against annual pretax profit after FIFO tax-loss carryforward. Losses carry forward for 5 years and no deferred tax assets are recognized.

debt_policy.design_note: General loans are enabled for sample testing. Auto borrowing remains disabled: negative cash should be visible as a warning rather than silently financed.

leverage_spread_model.design_note: Loan pricing uses the post-draw asset-liability ratio and linearly interpolates between spread-curve control points. If the beginning or post-draw ratio reaches 80%, the drawdown is blocked.

loan_rate_model.design_note: Loan rate v0.3 uses the regional annual policy rate for short-term turnover loans and the regional annual 10-year yield for long-term and grace construction loans. The fixed-at-draw quote preserves benchmark, product, term/grace, credit, leverage and boundary diagnostics; zero or negative policy rates remain valid inputs before the final 1.0%-9.5% clamp.
